title: From Student to Scientist
theme: Students move from REEF Campus orientation into the skills they'll apply in the field.

blocks.title: Welcome Program (arrival)
blocks.description: Students begin with a REEF Campus welcome and orientation that frames the trip as an immersive Florida Keys marine science experience.

blocks.title: Volunteer Fish Survey Project Training
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF volunteers identify fish and collect survey data, building the skills needed to participate in citizen science and marine biodiversity monitoring.

blocks.title: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a hands-on lesson and guided dissection, linking anatomy and adaptation to real conservation challenges in Florida Keys ecosystems.

studentsWill: Learn REEF's fish identification and survey methods before entering the field (Identify).
Investigate invasive lionfish anatomy and adaptation through a guided dissection (Understand).
Connect the lionfish investigation to REEF's ongoing invasive-species conservation work (Connect to Conservation).

title: Into the Field
theme: Students travel to real reef and coastal habitats to apply what they've learned.

blocks.title: Travel / Transit
blocks.description: Move between program locations with time built in for group transitions, preparation, and the next learning experience in the Florida Keys.

blocks.title: Kayaking (Mangrove Tour)
blocks.description: Students explore mangroves and seagrass by kayak while investigating how coastal habitats support marine life, protect shorelines, and fit into the larger reef ecosystem (Observe).

blocks.title: Boat Snorkel
blocks.description: Students travel by boat to the Florida Keys coral reef to practice fish identification, observe reef ecology in the field, and connect their observations to REEF citizen science (Observe → Connect to Conservation).

studentsWill: Investigate mangrove and seagrass habitats and how they shelter marine life (Observe).
Apply fish-ID skills on a real Florida Keys coral reef during a guided boat snorkel survey (Identify).
Record field observations that feed directly into REEF's Volunteer Fish Survey Project (Connect to Conservation).
outcomesNote: Boat and kayak activities are weather- and water-condition dependent.
